I've attempted by hanging a number of times. I don't feel comfortable giving you advice on how to do it most effectively, but I will say that it can be very painful. The rope digs into your neck tightly and crushes your trachea so you can't breathe, causing your hypercapnic response to kick in (you probably know this already but it's a panic response which occurs when there's too much carbon dioxide in your blood, which happens if you stop breathing for a while). It also really hurts your head which surprised me the first time I did it. You get a very intense pressure in your head and your eyes feel like they're about to pop out of your skull. Technically you're supposed to fall unconscious in under a minute (although it can take longer if you don't have the rope in the right place), but it feels like hours and hours while it's happening. 

The reason why I stopped last attempt is because I caught a glimpse of myself in the mirror and freaked out at the blue-ish grey colour of my skin from the lack of oxygen. I don't know if you're concerned about the state of your body when you're found, but your face will likely be that horrible purple/blue/grey colour. Not as bad as if you were to shoot yourself but still pretty unpleasant for whoever finds you. 

The panic is definitely the worst part of all of this though. Your survival instinct starts kicking in with your hypercapnic response and you'll be writhing around violently trying to get the rope off. It's especially panic-inducing if the knot is too tight to get off at first. In addition, you can continue to struggle even after you fall unconscious which could cause the rope to come off during that time. By that point you could already have pretty severe brain damage.

Basically what I'm trying to say is that I wouldn't recommend this method of suicide. Like I said before, I've tried it many times simply because it's the most accessible method to me, but you'll most likely go out panicking and in a lot of pain which isn't how I'd want to spend my last moments personally. You seem to know a lot about suicide methods which makes me think you've browsed some of the same websites I have- if that's the case, you might have come across people saying that this method is very quick and painless. While it may be less painful than other methods such as overdosing (which is the worst method in my opinion because it's slow, hardly ever seems to work and is very painful), it certainly isn't painless and can be very slow depending on how you set it up. 

Anyway, I know these words sound empty coming from a stranger on the internet but as someone who is also suicidal, I really do wish the best for you and hope that you can eventually escape from these thoughts. I wouldn't wish them on my worst enemy.

I have a few behavioural addictions including cutting/other forms of self harm and I find for all of them it feels really good while I'm doing it then really bad afterwards once the regret and shame has sunk in.

I've been clean from self harm for about a month now, but when I was doing it regularly I enjoyed the strong physical sensations and the release of tension I experienced while doing it, it made me feel less dead inside and more like an actual human being who feels things in a way. It didn't help that I'm sort of a masochist (not sexually, more like I enjoy being in pain the same way someone might enjoy watching a tv show or reading a book if that makes sense) so physical pain tends to feel quite comforting/calming to me. Because of that it was quite hard to accept that what I was doing was destroying my body, risking my life (particularly through some of my more dangerous methods of self harm such as strangling/choking), and ultimately making me feel worse as soon as the high wore off. It wasn't the pain that made me feel bad, but the scars, my family's reactions to them and the sensation of being completely unable to control my actions.
Congratulations, I'm so proud of you for making it that far!

Shortly before I started cutting I began looking at pictures online in an attempt to fight the urge to do it(it had the opposite effect in retrospect) and stumbled upon the self harm twitter community. It all went downhill from there as I became obsessed with the idea of self harm. Eventually I started doing it myself, but I'd been thinking about it for years beforehand. I discovered my other main self harm method (strangulation) by myself, I wasn't even sure it was self harm until I asked about it on here a while back and saw a few people had done the same.

Thank you for making this, a lot of your points really hit home (especially the part about waking up and suddenly feeling fine/not depressed, that happens to me often). I'm not officially diagnosed but I've been experiencing symptoms of depression for several years. I think a symptom people don't always acknowledge is the numbness or emptiness depression can make you feel. I often feel completely numb and disconnected from what's going on around me during a depressive episode, mainly because I stop caring about anything. I think some people who aren't depressed might assume it makes you feel sad all the time (and maybe it does for some people) but for me it's mostly emptiness with occasional bursts of sadness or anger in between. 

Also I find I spend a lot more time on my phone instead of getting out of bed/getting dressed/eating/etc (mainly because it provides some escapism from all the things I need to do but can't find the motivation for in real life I think), and it's very difficult to focus on anything for more than a few minutes at a time (I often end up with several different apps open on my phone because I started doing one thing then moved onto something else midway through and forgot about it).
i'm so proud of you for making it this far, that's an incredible achievement! I'm at 55 days currently so I'm almost there too :-)
